subject: Clarify AB sampling strategy & SLO thresholds for promptset rollout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify AB sampling strategy & SLO thresholds for promptset rollout

Team —

We need to lock the evaluation sampling and acceptance thresholds for the upcoming promptset A/B rollout to Acme (pilot). Product asks: we must provide a clear acceptance decision so Customer Success can sign off and Sales can move to canary. Open questions:

- Minimum per-variant sample size (per segment) to declare statistical significance for our primary quality metric (semantic accept rate).
- Whether we gate on absolute delta (e.g., >=1.5% worse) or relative degradation with respect to a rolling baseline.
- Canary cadence: how long to run and when to trigger rollback vs extend sampling.
- Any customer-facing guardrails (e.g., immediate fallback to previous model on hallucination or PII exposures).

Attached: sampling_matrix_v1.csv (proposed strata) and slo_proposal.pdf (rough thresholds). Related links: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1aBcEvalPlan and JIRA-EVAL-457.

Context: Acme will seed with 5k weekly active test users across two segments (enterprise / self-serve). They want a short canary (48-72h) but legal wants us to be conservative. We should propose a plan that balances cost, lead time, and risk.

Ask: Marissa — can you sketch the concrete numbers (sample size, metric definition, gating rule) by noon PT? Aditya — can you confirm telemetry availability (latency / failure / hallucination signals) and if cost constraints require sampling limits? Grace — product/CS alignment; please confirm what level of regression is acceptable to Acme and whether they require immediate fallback thresholds.

Thanks,
Karthik
Lead, Eval Orchestration
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AB sampling strategy & SLO thresholds for promptset rollout

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear ask. High-level proposal below (I expanded the sampling_matrix_v1 to concrete numbers):

- Primary metric: semantic_accept_rate (SAR) defined as % of rubric-labeled responses rated acceptable by our evals panel for the customer’s top-10 intents. Secondary: hallucination_rate (binary per-response) and median latency (ms).
- Minimum per-variant sample size: 2,400 labeled responses per variant per segment for SAR to detect ~1.5 percentage-point absolute difference with 80% power (approx; see attached calc notes). For smaller segments (self-serve <1k users), use pooled sampling and raise the canary duration.
- Gating rule: fail if absolute SAR delta <= -1.5pp AND hallucination_rate delta >= +0.4pp, OR median latency increase > 100ms. In other words, we require both a quality regression and a complementary signal before blocking.
- Canary cadence: start with 72h window + 24h buffered review. If metrics are close to threshold (within 0.5pp), extend sampling to 7 days.
- Fallback: immediate traffic switch to previous model variant if hallucination_rate spikes > 1.5pp absolute vs baseline (customer-facing).

Notes/questions for product/CS: Grace — is Acme comfortable with the pooled approach for self-serve? Sarah (Cc) — would Acme accept the fallback rule above for the pilot?

Next steps: I’ll push an updated sampling_matrix_v2.csv and a short calc sheet to the Drive link. Assuming we accept these numbers, owners: Marissa (sampling), Aditya (telemetry), Karthik (final gate definition + doc).

—Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Eval Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@acme.com>
Date: 2028-06-01T13:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AB sampling strategy & SLO thresholds for promptset rollout

+1 to Marissa’s approach. Some operational notes:

- Telemetry: we have per-request hallucination_score, response_tokens, and plain error/timeout counters in the model pipeline. Live stream available for the canary; historical baseline is on Drive (link in thread).
- Cost: labeling 2,400 responses per variant/segment is ~18k labels for the pilot (two variants x two segments). That’s within budget but we should confirm with Finance for extended runs. If cost becomes an issue, we can use prioritized sampling (focus on top intents + low-confidence outputs) to reduce labels to ~9k while preserving power on key intents.
- Canary routing: propose phased ramp — 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 24-72h with the full 72h sampling window starting once we hit 25% traffic. That gives an early abort opportunity.

Action items I can take on:
- Set up telemetry dashboard and a live stream hook for the sampling cohort (JIRA-EVAL-457).
- Add prioritized-sampling script to save labeling budget; will add flags to the sampling matrix.

Links: Drive eval artifacts (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1aBcEvalPlan), JIRA-EVAL-457.

Aditya
Staff ML Engineer, Inference Telemetry
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-06-01T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify AB sampling strategy & SLO thresholds for promptset rollout

Thanks all — this reads sensible and aligns with CS risk tolerance for the pilot. Quick answers:

- Acme confirmed they’re OK with pooled sampling for the smaller self-serve segment as long as we disclose the limitation in the post-canary writeup.
- They want explicit rollback criteria for hallucination spikes (your threshold is fine).
- They requested a proactive customer notification if we extend sampling beyond 72h.

I’ll file the customer sign-off note in the Drive folder and update the mutual action plan with the fallback language. Marissa/Aditya/Karthik — please paste the final gating snippet into the MAP by EOD so Sales can start the canary ramp tomorrow morning.

—Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
